record_identity.title: Gemini image-generation tuning produced historically inaccurate depictions and over-broad refusals

incident_identity.date_basis: AIID records 21 February 2024 for the incident cluster; Google paused people-image generation and published its postmortem on 23 February 2024.

summary: Google paused Gemini's generation of images of people after users surfaced historically inaccurate and offensive outputs. Google later explained that diversity tuning failed to account for contexts where diversity should not be introduced and that the model also became more cautious than intended, refusing some benign prompts.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: Google states that its tuning to produce diverse people did not correctly distinguish historical or otherwise specific contexts and that the model overcompensated. Google temporarily disabled people-image generation and committed to further testing. AIID Incident 645 aggregates 35 reports around the same failure cluster.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: A protective and diversity-oriented control became operative in contexts where its valid conditions were not satisfied and also over-triggered refusals on benign requests. This is a strong example of a safeguard/tuning objective activating outside its appropriate scope.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: The occurrence provides a historical non-OpenAI example of over-broad governance-control activation and is directly relevant to Caelestis work on proportionality, trigger conditions and avoiding protective overreach.
assessment_boundaries: The record does not treat diversity objectives themselves as a failure; the failure is the control's application in contexts where Google says it should not have applied.
The Incident does not adjudicate political claims about bias beyond Google's own acknowledgement of inaccurate historical outputs and over-conservative refusals.
Individual affected users and downstream reliance are not quantified.

This satisfies VIGIL-FC-000043 Unwarranted Control Activation.

severity_assessment.materialised_consequence: Gemini generated inaccurate or offensive historical people images and refused some benign prompts; Google paused the people-image feature globally while it reworked the system.
severity_assessment.affected_scope: Public Gemini users of people-image generation during the affected February 2024 deployment; the number of affected prompts or users is not published.
severity_assessment.seriousness_and_persistence: The incident created material information-integrity and product-governance harm and required a global feature pause, but no severe individual physical, financial or rights harm is established.
severity_assessment.quantitative_information: AIID aggregates 35 incident reports; Google did not publish a count of affected prompts or users.
severity_assessment.evidentiary_limits: The record does not treat diversity objectives themselves as a failure; the failure is the control's application in contexts where Google says it should not have applied. The Incident does not adjudicate political claims about bias beyond Google's own acknowledgement of inaccurate historical outputs and over-conservative refusals. Individual affected users and downstream reliance are not quantified.
severity_assessment.band_rationale: S3 rather than S2 is appropriate because serious persistent individual harm is not established. S3 rather than S4 is appropriate because the failure affected a globally deployed feature, produced materially inaccurate outputs and required the provider to disable people-image generation.
